approach: Add one prose paragraph to the change producer prompt (crates/athena-cap-change/prompts/producer.md), between the existing study-claim text and the closing "Before you report" sentence, which becomes its own last paragraph. The paragraph gives the producer what the four failed jobs lacked. For an intermittent or racy failure it must first reproduce it under load with a test that loops the action on threads and counts failures, using crates/athena-testkit/tests/stand_in_stress.rs as the worked example (the Bash policy denies shell loops). It names the cause in code terms and fixes it where it starts. If several sites share the cause it fixes them in one shared helper and adds a repo test that finds every site and fails with the cause put back. It reports the command and the counts before and after. A unit test in crates/athena-cap-change/src/lib.rs pins each element inside that paragraph, pins the report step as the last paragraph, checks the named example file exists, and checks that the live producer command list names no shell program, so the prompt's denial claim stays true. The larger prompt moves the computed producer set size, so one number in docs/system-facts.md changes because the budget drift test requires it. CHANGELOG.md gets one entry and docs/decisions.md gets D189, which names the planner frame as a stage that also lacked this guidance and proposes a follow-up. No refusal rule, gate or job step is added: 0% of past accepted readings are refused. The testkit helper, scan, stress test and drain.rs fix from the earlier jobs are in the tree and are not touched.

decisions.choice: Put the missing guidance in the change capability's own producer section as one prose paragraph pinned by a unit test. The text (one line, no list marker): 'For an intermittent or racy failure, first reproduce it under load with a test that loops the action on threads and counts failures (see crates/athena-testkit/tests/stand_in_stress.rs; the Bash policy denies shell loops). Name the cause in code terms; fix it where it starts. If sites share it, fix them in one shared helper and add a repo test that finds every site and fails with the cause put back. Report the command and counts before and after.' Keep 'fix it where it starts' unconditional; make the shared helper and the all-sites test conditional on 'If sites share it'.
decisions.reason: The failing stage lacked information, not permission: nothing in its brief said how to reproduce a flake under load, how to state a cause, how to fix a repeated pattern once, or that the evidence must be reported. The request prefers giving information over a refusal rule. The section is compiled in by include_str! at crates/athena-cap-change/src/lib.rs:21 and returned by Change.producer_section() (lib.rs:51); the existing tests module (lib.rs:118) is where the test goes. Finding 2 (critic, major): the guidance had dropped the report clause. The last sentence now says 'Report the command and counts before and after', and the test pins it. 'Before and after' covers the post-fix soak, because the same loop is run on the fixed tree. This closes the 9daz gap (no recorded loop), where a producer could run the loop and show nothing. The method is a loop in one test on threads, because the producer's Bash policy splits at && ; | and newlines and requires each program on the role's list (crates/athena-agent/src/policy.rs:6-10), and athena.toml:84 lists only cargo, git, ls, rm, mv and chmod for the change producer, so a for or seq loop is denied. The worked example has writer threads, loop cycles and forker threads that add fork/exec load while counting failures (stand_in_stress.rs:13-15, 24-67). The 9daz flake in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs was a single-site race, so the helper and the scan stay conditional on several sites.

decisions.reason: The facts file says producer 1043 of 1200. The set size is ceil(bytes/3) over the composed text (crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs:74-76, compose at :143-154), so the base is 3127 to 3129 bytes and the hard limit is 3600. check_budget fails only when the estimate is over the budget (lib.rs:226-235). The addition is 449+3 = 452 bytes, giving 3579 to 3581 bytes, which is 1193 or 1194 tokens (an estimate), about 6 below the budget. This is tighter than the earlier 418-byte draft because finding 2 added the report clause and finding 3 asked for the full path. A cap of 450 keeps at least 5 tokens of room for the next edit to this file. The reader brief computes the room at run time (headroom_rows, lib.rs:258-263), and a Grep for 157 and 1043 finds no other static copy of the figure.
